snapforge.name: SnapForge 0.2.0
snapforge.body:
### Added

- **Beautify** (Effects menu, the ✨ button, or `Ctrl+B`): puts a screenshot on a padded
  background with rounded corners and a soft shadow, in one step. Choose one of eight
  gradients, a solid color or a transparent background, and optionally pad the result to
  16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4 or 9:16. The preview updates as you change the values.
- **Hide Private Details** (Tools menu, the 🙈 button, or `Ctrl+Shift+H`): SnapForge reads
  the text in the picture and covers every e-mail address, phone number and payment card
  number it finds, with pixels, a blur or a black bar. Each cover is a normal annotation
  that you can move, resize or delete, and one Undo removes them all. With a selection,
  only the selection is checked. Everything happens on your PC.
- **Read QR Code** (Tools menu, the 🔳 button, or `Ctrl+Shift+Q`): shows what the QR codes
  in the picture (or in the selection) say, with Copy and Open Link buttons.
- **Capture Text also reads QR codes**: when the captured area contains a QR code, its
  content appears above the recognized text. This works even when no OCR language is
  installed.
- **Capture History** (Tools menu, tray menu, or `Ctrl+H` in the editor): the most recent captures are kept and can
  be found again, including captures that only went to the clipboard. Search by date,
  size, capture type, file name or by words that appear in the picture. Open a capture
  in the editor, copy it, show it in its folder or remove it. The number of captures kept
  (50 by default) and an off switch are in Settings ▸ Capture History.
- **Right-to-left names**: Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew file names are drawn
  correctly (joined letters, right order) on the editor's tabs and in Capture History.
- A **Share-ready** group on the editor toolbar with Beautify, Hide Private Details and
  Read QR Code.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (this file).

### Changed

- **Exit asks first** when pictures in the editor have changes that were never saved.
  Closing the editor window only hides it, so these pictures used to be lost without a
  word when you chose Exit.
- Cropping a picture that has annotations is now **one Undo step** (it used to take two,
  and after the first one the annotations sat in the wrong place).
- A capture started from the command line that opens the editor now leaves a complete
  SnapForge running (tray icon, toolbar and hotkeys), not a half-started one.
- Relative paths given on the command line (`--open a.png`, `--file shot.png`) are
  resolved in the folder you ran the command from, also when SnapForge is already running.
- `--file` with a name that is not an image file (no or unknown extension) is rejected
  with a message, instead of saving nothing and reporting success.
- `scripts/package.ps1` and the installer script use `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when it is set.

### Fixed

- **Captures taken within the same second no longer replace each other.** With the
  default file name (one name per second), repeated or scripted captures could get the
  same name, and the later one silently replaced the earlier one.
- **Effects on a pasted or moved piece that hangs over the edge of the picture** did
  nothing ("no change"). The selection is now cut to the picture when the piece is merged.
- **Edit ▸ Paste, the right-click Paste and the command palette** could not paste copied
  annotations (only `Ctrl+V` could).
- **Settings could be saved out of order** when several changes came close together, which
  could leave an older state on disk. Settings are also written when Windows shuts down or
  you sign out.
- **Capture Text window**: `Esc` closes the window again after you clicked Copy All, Copy
  Selected or Keep line breaks, and when recognition failed. A maximized window no longer
  overwrites the remembered window size.
- The `###` counter in file names no longer skips numbers when a capture is sent by
  e-mail, to an Office program or uploaded, or when a pin's Save As dialog is cancelled.
- User guide: the Hotkeys and File names sections described editing `settings.toml`;
  they now describe the Settings window. The README said full screen captures the
  "active" monitor; it is the monitor under the pointer.

reelforge.name: ReelForge 1.1.0
reelforge.body:
### Added
- **Drop a subtitle file on the window** (`.srt`, `.ass`, `.ssa`, `.vtt`) and it is burned into the video with the same name, or into the selected video. Subtitle files can also be picked together with the videos in *Add files*.
- **Size saved in the finish line**: "Finished: 3 converted in 01:20 · 1.2 GB → 410 MB (66% smaller)".
- **Time left** for the whole conversion next to the progress bar, and the **progress in the window title**, so it shows on the taskbar while ReelForge is in the background.
- **Right-click a file** for a menu: Edit, Play the original, Show the original in its folder, Show the converted file, Conversion log, Remove from the list. **Double-click** a file to edit it.
- **Keyboard shortcuts**: `Ctrl+O` add files, `↑` `↓` select, `Enter` edit, `Delete` remove, `Ctrl+A` tick all, `Esc` close the open window.
- **Clear done** button: takes the converted files off the list and keeps the rest.
- **Cancel shutdown** button after a conversion that ends with *Shut down when done*.
- **Type a time** in the trim boxes: `1:30`, `0:01:30.5` or `90`. Times that are not whole seconds now show their tenths.
- The file list shows which files have subtitles switched on.

### Changed
- **Kurdish and Arabic text is now drawn by Windows itself**, the way File Explorer draws it. File names, track titles, subtitle names, folders, messages and the conversion log are joined and ordered correctly, including the Kurdish letters ڕ ڵ ە ێ, which used to stand apart.
- **Convert carries on where it stopped.** After a stop or a failed file, pressing Convert again only does the files that are not done yet. When every ticked file is already done, it converts them all again as before.
- Files are read four at a time when you add them, so adding a folder with hundreds of files no longer starts hundreds of background programs at once.
- Long file names are cut with "…" instead of running into the status on the right.
- The overall progress bar counts only the files of the conversion that is running, weighed by their length after trimming.
- *Clear* is greyed out while converting instead of silently doing nothing.
- The About window shows the real version number and lists the shortcuts.
- `scripts\package.ps1` builds into `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when it is set.

### Fixed
- **Two files with the same name** (from different folders) converted at the same time were written to the same output file. Each now gets its own name.
- **The original could be overwritten** when "Next to the original" and "Overwrite" were both on and the name differed only in upper/lower case (for example `CLIP.MP4` → `clip.mp4`). The original is never written over now.
- **Stop no longer shuts the computer down.** With *Shut down when done* ticked, pressing Stop after at least one file had finished still turned the computer off, and still opened the output folder.
- **No more broken half-files.** A stopped or failed conversion left an unplayable partial file behind. It is now removed (a file that was there before the conversion is never deleted).
- With "Next to the original", the folder opened at the end is the one the files really went to, a merged file is saved next to the first original, and the unused output folder is no longer created.
- The finish line counted files converted in earlier runs as well.

unforge.name: UnForge 1.1.0
unforge.body:
### Added

- **Browser extensions** tab: every add-on installed in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera and Firefox, for every profile, with version, size and whether it is switched off. Each one has a button to show its files and one to open its store page. UnForge only lists extensions; it does not remove them.
- **Changes** tab: UnForge notes the list of installed programs each time it is opened and shows what was installed, updated or removed in between. A program that is still installed can be uninstalled straight from that list.
- **"Still running" warning** before an uninstall: if the program is open, the Prepare step names what is running from its install folder and offers **Close them now** and **Check again**. An open program is the usual reason an uninstaller fails or leftover files cannot be deleted.
- **Right-click menu** on every program: Uninstall, Forced uninstall, add to the selection, Open install folder, Open in Registry Editor, Search online, Copy name, Copy details.
- **Right-click menu on leftovers** in the review step: open the folder, show the file in its folder, or open the key in Registry Editor before you decide, and copy its path.
- **Keyboard control of the list**: arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End move the highlight, Space ticks a program, Enter starts the uninstall, Ctrl+A ticks everything that is shown.
- **Taskbar and Quick Launch pins** that open a file in the install folder are now found as leftovers.
- **Export as JSON**, next to CSV and HTML.

### Changed

- A folder or key whose name differs from the program's only by a symbol (a plain name next to one ending in `++` or `#`) is now Likely instead of Safe, so it is shown but not ticked for you.
- The selection bar counts every ticked program and says how many are hidden by the current search or filter.
- Confirmation dialogs keep their buttons in a fixed-height row, which rules out a layout fault that can stretch a dialog down the window.

### Fixed

- **Batch uninstall skipped ticked programs** that the current search or filter was hiding, although the button counted them. Everything that is ticked is now uninstalled.
- **Leftovers shared with another installed version were ticked as Safe.** When another version or edition of the same program stays installed (a 3.11 next to a 3.12, or the 32-bit next to the 64-bit one), folders and registry keys that carry only the shared name are now shown as Unsure in a Deep scan, unticked, and the reason names the version that still uses them.
- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew** names and paths were drawn as separate letters in the wrong order. The program list, the details panel and the uninstall steps now show them joined up and right to left.
- `scripts\package.ps1` and the installer script now work when cargo's output folder is set with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

**Downloads**

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `UnForge-Setup.exe` | Installer with Start Menu and desktop shortcuts and an uninstaller |
| `UnForge-1.1.0-portable-x64.zip` | Portable: unzip and run, nothing is installed |
| `UnForge.exe` | The bare EXE |

Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/zheerkhalid/unforge/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

keepforge.name: KeepForge 1.1.0
keepforge.body:
Vaults made with 1.0.x open as they are; nothing about the vault file or its encryption has changed.

### Added

- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew text is shown properly.** Titles, user names, folders, tags, field names, notes and the vault name on the lock screen are now drawn with joined letters and in the right reading order. Before, the letters stood apart and ran backwards.
- **Sort the item list** by title, by what changed most recently, or by what was added most recently (the new button next to *New*). The choice is remembered.
- **Move through the list with the keyboard.** Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End walk the list, also while the search box is active, and Enter picks the first search result. So: `Ctrl+F`, type, Down, `Ctrl+C`.
- **Drag a file onto the window** to store it as an attachment of the item that is open.
- **The generator remembers what you copied.** The last 8 passwords copied from the Generator page are listed there, in case one went into a sign-up form before you saved it. They are kept in memory only and are gone when the vault locks.
- **Unencrypted web addresses in the security dashboard.** Logins whose saved address starts with `http://` are listed, because the password travels without encryption. Devices at home (router pages, `localhost`, private addresses) are left out.
- **Three more CSV export layouts are recognised on import**, including secure notes, payment cards and identities that used to arrive as plain logins or lose their folder, favourite mark or one-time code.
- **The trash can empty itself.** A new setting removes items that have been in the trash for 30 days, 90 days or a year. It is off unless you turn it on.
- **The lock screen says why it locked** ("Locked after 5 minutes without activity", "Locked because Windows was locked or went to sleep"). The short message shown before was gone by the time you came back.

### Changed

- Checking an import for duplicates is fast now, also with thousands of entries. Before, a large import into a large vault could freeze the window for a long time.
- A CSV file that only has web address, user name and password columns no longer uses the user name as the title; the site name is used.
- While you type a Kurdish or Arabic title, a "Shown as" line under the box shows how it will look (the text box itself still shows the letters unjoined).
- The demo vault (`KeepForge.exe --demo`) has an item written in Kurdish.
- For people who build KeepForge themselves: `scripts\package.ps1` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

### Fixed

- The item list jumped slightly while scrolling and could be scrolled past its last item into an empty area.
- CSV import: a semicolon-separated file with a comma inside a quoted heading, or with an empty first line, was read as one single column.

shredforge.name: ShredForge 1.1.0
shredforge.body:
### Added

- **Schedule.** A new Schedule page lets Windows start a job by itself, every day, every week or every month, even when ShredForge is closed: shred the Recycle Bin, wipe the free space of a drive, or shred everything inside one folder (the folder itself stays). You confirm once, when you create the schedule; every run leaves a report, and a run that was missed starts as soon as possible. Whole drives can never be scheduled, and the usual safety rules apply to every run.
- **Small drop window.** "Small window" on the Files and folders page (or Ctrl+M) shrinks ShredForge to a small window that stays on top of your other windows. Drop files on it from anywhere; nothing is shredded until you open the list and confirm.
- **Paste paths.** Copy files in Explorer with "Copy as path" and press Ctrl+V on the Files and folders page to add them to the list.
- **Advice for SSDs and USB sticks in the confirmation.** ShredForge now tells you whether the drive supports TRIM and whether Windows has TRIM switched on (that is what really clears flash memory after a file is deleted), and warns when the chosen algorithm writes many passes, which only wears a flash drive.
- **Verification in the report.** When files are read back after shredding, the report now says how many files were checked and how many matched, instead of only the amount of data.
- **Command line:** `--shred-contents <folder> --yes` shreds everything inside a folder and keeps the folder. `--run-schedule` and `--remove-schedules` are used by the Schedule page and the uninstaller.
- This changelog, also included in the installer and the portable ZIP.

### Changed

- Folders get their dates reset to 1 January 1980 before they are renamed and removed, the same as files, so the leftover record says nothing about when the folder was used.
- The Reports page picks up reports written by scheduled jobs while the window is open.
- Uninstalling ShredForge removes its scheduled jobs from Windows.
- Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+8 switch pages (Schedule is the new fifth page).

### Fixed

- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew file names** were drawn as separate letters in the wrong order. They now appear joined and right to left, as in Explorer, in the list, the confirmation, the progress view and the reports.
- **Files with a second name (hard links)** now get the warning the README always promised: the report says that the shared data was overwritten and that the other name now leads to an empty file.
- **Free space wipe on a compressed drive.** With an algorithm that writes zeros, Windows compressed the temporary files to almost nothing, so the free space was never really filled. The temporary folder is now kept uncompressed.
- The progress bar could jump backwards while shredding files that carry alternate data streams (for example files downloaded from the internet).

bootforge.name: BootForge 1.1.0
bootforge.body:
### Added

- **Windows Setup options.** When you make a drive from a Windows setup image in file-copy mode,
  three new switches appear under Options:
  - *Windows 11 checks* skips the TPM 2.0, Secure Boot and memory checks, so that Windows 11 Setup
    continues on a PC that does not meet those requirements (Windows 11 images only).
  - *Local account* makes the first start ask for a local user name instead of a Microsoft
    account, and work without an internet connection.
  - *Privacy questions* answers the location, diagnostics and advertising questions with "no"
    and does not show them.

  BootForge does this by adding one small answer file (`autounattend.xml`) to the drive. The files
  of the image are not changed, the added file is verified like every other file, and deleting it
  from the drive gives the plain Windows Setup back. The confirmation dialog and the result page
  say which options were applied. Images that bring an answer file of their own keep it, and the
  options are not offered for them.
- **Checksum files are found for you.** If the folder of an image also holds the checksum file its
  publisher provides (`SHA256SUMS`, `sha256sum.txt`, `MD5SUMS`, `image.iso.sha256` and similar),
  BootForge reads the value listed for your image. The Checksums page fills it in, and the image
  card on the Create page offers "Check the image against it now" and then shows either
  "Checksum verified" or a clear warning that the download is damaged.
- **Recent images.** The empty Create page lists the last five images you used; one click selects
  an image again. Entries whose file is gone are removed when clicked.
- **The taskbar button flashes when a job ends** while you are working in another window.
- **Command line:** `BootForge.exe --hash <file> --expect <checksum>` compares and ends with exit
  code 2 when the file does not match (useful in scripts). Without `--expect`, a checksum file
  next to the file is used when there is one. `BootForge.exe --version` prints the version.
- The built-in self-test (`--selftest`) now also writes a drive image with the Windows Setup
  options switched on and reads the answer file back.

### Changed

- **The PC no longer goes to sleep while a job runs.** Writing, verifying, backing up and the
  bad-block check keep Windows awake until they have finished (the screen may still switch off).
- The Windows Setup choices are remembered and offered again for the next Windows image.
- The window opens a little taller (1280 x 860) so that all options of a Windows image fit
  without scrolling.
- The packaging script (`scripts/package.ps1`) uses the folder named in `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when
  that is set, and removes portable zips of earlier versions from `dist`.

### Fixed

- **Restarting as administrator lost an image given with a relative path.** Starting BootForge
  with `--image some.iso` from a folder and then pressing "Restart as administrator" opened the
  elevated window without the image, because Windows starts elevated programs in another folder.
  The path is now made complete at start.
- **Needless redrawing during steps without a known length.** While a step with no byte count
  was running (a quick format, for example), every progress update was passed on at once instead
  of at most twenty times a second, which kept the window busy for nothing.

wireforge.name: WireForge 1.1.0
wireforge.body:
**New: a simple app firewall, built on Windows Defender Firewall.**

- **Firewall page**: status of each network profile, the apps WireForge blocks (with time left), the other rules that affect an app (read-only), a journal of changes with undo, and "Remove all WireForge rules".
- **Block an app in one click** from the Apps or Connections page (button or right-click): for 1 hour, until restart or always; outgoing, optionally incoming; all or chosen networks.
- **New-app alerts** (optional, off by default): Allow or Block the first time a program connects to the internet; answers are remembered and editable.
- **Lockdown** (optional, clearly warned): block all outgoing traffic except an allow list; ending it restores the previous defaults exactly. An "End lockdown" button stays at the top of the window.
- Administrator permission is asked only for each change (an elevated `WireForge.exe --fw-...` command). Command line: `--fw-list`, `--fw-block <exe>`, `--fw-unblock <exe>`, `--fw-lockdown on|off`, `--fw-undo`, `--fw-remove-all`.
- The uninstaller offers to remove WireForge's firewall rules.

Honest note: the firewall logic is covered by unit tests against an in-memory firewall, and reading the real firewall was tested. Adding and removing real rules, the elevation prompt, scheduled task expiry and lockdown were not exercised on a real PC before this release. See "How the firewall works" in the README.

twinforge.name: TwinForge 1.1.0
twinforge.body:
### Added

- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew names are shown correctly.** File and folder names in right-to-left scripts are now drawn joined and in the right order, the same way File Explorer shows them: in the results, the compare panel, the folder list, the confirmation, the report and the history.
- **"Not a match": hide a group for good.** Right-click a group (or use the button in the compare panel) to hide it. The group leaves the list and stays hidden in later scans, until a new file joins it. Nothing is deleted. *Settings → Hidden groups → Show them again* brings everything back.
- **Large compare window for pictures.** *Enlarge* in the compare panel opens the two pictures side by side at a size where differences can be seen, with *Keep this one*, *Keep the other* and *Not a match*. Up and Down move through the list while it is open.
- **iPhone and camera pictures.** Similar pictures now also reads HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, JPEG XL and camera RAW files (DNG, CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW, ORF, RW2, RAF, PEF, SRW, NRW), using the picture codecs of Windows. Some of these need a free extension from the Microsoft Store (HEIF Image Extensions, AV1 Video Extension, Raw Image Extension); without it the file is listed as "not read".
- **New keep-rule: "Keep the original name".** Keeps the file whose name does not look like a copy, such as `photo (1).jpg`, `report - Copy.docx` or `Copy of budget.xlsx`, and selects the others. Also on the command line: `--keep original-name`.
- **"Keep the copies in this folder".** Right-click a file: in every group that has a copy in that folder, that copy stays and the others are selected.
- **Right-click menu for groups:** *Select all but the first*, *Clear this group*, *Hide this group from now on*.
- **Drag and drop:** drop folders on the window to add them to the places to scan (a dropped file stands for its folder).
- **Keyboard:** Left and Right close and open the highlighted group.

### Changed

- Similar music treats Kurdish, Arabic and Persian tags as the same text when they only differ in how they were typed (ي / ی, ك / ک, ە / ه, with or without vowel marks), and reads Arabic and Persian digits as numbers.
- A picture in a variant the built-in decoder does not support gets a second try with the Windows codecs before it is reported as unreadable. Damaged files are still reported, never half-read.
- The "Everything in a folder" menu and the "scanning now" line show right-to-left paths correctly too.
- `scripts\package.ps1` and the installer script build from `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when it is set.

### Fixed

- With the "With selection" or "Without selection" filter on, the list did not follow Ctrl+A, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+D or "Keep this one"; groups that no longer fitted the filter stayed visible until something else refreshed the list.
- Keyboard shortcuts no longer reach the list behind an open dialog. Before, pressing Enter while the confirmation was showing opened the highlighted file, and Space or Ctrl+A changed the selection behind it.


Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/zheerkhalid/twinforge/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

rescueforge.name: RescueForge 1.1.0
rescueforge.body:
### Added

- **Continue a stopped deep scan.** When you stop a deep scan, RescueForge remembers how far it got. A "Continue scan" button picks it up at the same place instead of starting over, and the files already listed and your ticks are kept. The position is also stored in saved sessions, so a long scan can be spread over several days: stop, save with Ctrl+S, open the session later and continue.
- **23 more kinds of file found by a deep scan** (66 kinds in all): JPEG 2000, DjVu, EMF drawings, icons and cursors, MPEG video (MPG, VOB), WavPack, Monkey's Audio, DSD, AMR voice recordings and AU audio, contacts (vCard) and calendars (iCalendar), Zstandard, LZ4 and Debian packages, fonts (TTF, OTF, WOFF, WOFF2), Flash, Windows shortcuts, registry hives and event logs, Linux programs and libraries, and network captures. As before, the real end of each file is worked out from its structure.
- **Previews for more files:**
  - Camera RAW photos (CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG and others) and Photoshop files show the picture stored inside them, also as thumbnails in the grid.
  - Songs (MP3, FLAC, M4A, WMA) show their cover picture.
  - Word, PowerPoint, Excel and OpenDocument files show their text, so you can tell which document is which before recovering.
  - ZIP archives (also JAR, APK, EPUB) list the files inside them.
  - Text files saved in the older Windows encodings (for example Arabic or Western European "ANSI") are shown as text instead of raw bytes.
- **Right-click menu on every file** in the list and in the thumbnail grid: recover this file, open the large preview, tick it, tick all files of the same type, tick everything in its folder, copy the name or the original path.
- **Export the list** of found files as a table (CSV) for Excel or any spreadsheet, with Ctrl+E or the "Export list" button: the ticked files, or everything shown. Like every other write, it is refused on the drive being scanned.
- **Search with several words and patterns.** `holiday 2025` finds names that contain both words; `*.jpg` or `img_20??.*` match whole names.
- **"Clear filters"** button next to the filters, and a **"Show everything"** button when no file matches.
- More keys: Page Up / Page Down, Home / End, and the arrow keys move tile by tile in the thumbnail grid.

### Changed

- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian, Urdu and Hebrew are now drawn by Windows itself**, the same way File Explorer does: letters join and the text reads right to left. This covers file and folder names everywhere (list, grid, folder tree, details, recovery report) and the text preview.
- Stopping a deep scan now still lists the files of an earlier file system (from before a format) that were found up to that point. Before, they were dropped unless the scan ran to the end.
- The scan log says where a continued scan started and counts what was found since.
- The file-type list in Settings is longer; every new type can be switched off there.

### Fixed

- Kurdish and Arabic file names appeared as separate, unjoined letters in the wrong order.
- Moving through the list with the arrow keys could move the highlight out of sight: the list now scrolls with it.
- A very long file name that was shortened for recovery could end in a space or a dot, which Windows does not allow.
- The "No files match" message was a dead end; it now offers the way back.

### Not changed, on purpose

- The scanned drive, disk or image is still only ever opened for reading, and nothing is ever saved onto it.
- Session files from 1.0 open in 1.1 (they simply have no position to continue from).


Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/zheerkhalid/rescueforge/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

spaceforge.name: SpaceForge 1.1.0
spaceforge.body:
### Added

- **Cleanup page.** A new page lists what is usually safe to remove: what is left in the temporary folders, program caches, crash dumps and old logs, downloads you have not touched for three months, and large files unchanged for a year. It only makes suggestions: nothing is ticked for you, and what you tick goes to the Recycle Bin after you confirm. The list can be exported as a CSV table.
- **What grew since last time.** SpaceForge now remembers each scan by itself. Scan a drive again later and the Drives page says how much it grew or shrank since the scan before, with one click to see exactly which folders changed. The last two scans of each drive or folder are kept; this can be turned off in Settings.
- **Recycle Bin at a glance.** The Cleanup page shows how much the Recycle Bin holds and opens it, since emptying it is what actually frees the space.
- **Drag and drop.** Drop a folder or a drive on the window to scan it, or a snapshot file to compare with it.
- **Command line:** `--cleanup <file.csv>` writes the cleanup suggestions of a scan to a file. It never deletes anything.
- **Ctrl+9** opens the Cleanup page.

### Changed

- Comparing a snapshot with the scan in the window now looks only at the drives and folders both contain. If they have nothing in common, SpaceForge says so instead of showing an empty or misleading result.
- When an item cannot go to the Recycle Bin because its path is longer than 260 characters, the message now says so and points to permanent delete.
- The packaging script builds into the folder named by `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when that is set.

### Fixed

- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew names** were shown with separated letters in the wrong order. They are now drawn joined up and right to left, in the folder tree, the lists, the treemap, the search results, the comparison and the dialogs.
- Comparing a snapshot of one drive with a scan of several drives listed the other drives as "new", and their whole size as growth.
- The two snapshots picked for a comparison could silently change to different ones when the snapshot list was reloaded, for example after saving a new snapshot.

findforge.name: FindForge 1.1.0
findforge.body:
### Added

- **Look inside files.** Add `content:invoice` (or `content:"total due"`) to a search and FindForge opens the plain-text files that match the rest of the search and keeps the ones that contain the text. It only happens when you ask for it, so ordinary searches stay instant. It also works from the command line: `FindForge.exe -s "content:invoice ext:txt;csv"`.
- While files are being read the status bar says so, and afterwards it tells how many files were looked into and how many were skipped. The index keeps following your drives in the meantime.
- The preview pane marks the text that `content:` found.
- **Matches are highlighted in Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew names**, just as in other names.
- **Open with…** in the actions menu (the ⋯ button), to pick the program a result opens in.
- The window remembers its size, and whether it was maximized, for the next start.

### Changed

- Searches that take more than a second show their time in seconds instead of thousands of milliseconds.
- Right-to-left names are no longer drawn again while you resize a column, unless they have to be cut shorter.
- The packaging script works with a build folder outside the project (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`).

### Fixed

- **Kurdish and Arabic text typed in the search box is now shown joined and in the right order.** The caret, the selection and mouse clicks land on the right letters. The same goes for the rename box, the filter and bookmark boxes and the lists in Settings.

Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/zheerkhalid/findforge/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

hourforge.name: HourForge 1.1.0
hourforge.body:
Your recorded time and your settings from 1.0.0 are used as they are. Nothing needs converting.

### Added

- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew text is shown properly.** Window titles, project and client names, notes, tags and categories in these scripts now appear joined and in the right reading order everywhere: the timeline, Today, reports, the Projects page, menus and drop-down lists. You can also type them in every text box (search, notes, project names, the timer task) and see them correctly while typing.
- **Review page.** A new page lists the programs and websites that no rule has sorted yet, the ones with the most time first. Pick a category once and HourForge remembers it. Websites that only count as "Browsing" because of the browser they were opened in are listed too. A number next to "Review" shows how many are waiting.
- **Invoice.** On the Projects page, "Invoice…" makes a clean page to print or save as PDF: your name, the client, one line per project with hours, rate and amount, the total due, and the hours per day behind it. Also from the command line: `HourForge.exe --export last-month --invoice`.
- **Billable switch for projects.** Mark a project as not billable to keep tracking it without ever charging it: it shows no amount on timesheets and is left off invoices.
- **Calendar export.** The activity report can be saved as a calendar file (.ics) for Outlook, Google Calendar and others, with one event per sitting, named after its project or category. Window titles and websites are left out of the file on purpose. Command line: `--format ics`.
- **Weekly summary.** At the start of each week a notice near the clock tells you last week's hours, how that compares with the week before, and your busiest category and project. Clicking it opens that week in the reports. It can be turned off in Settings.
- **Search in the timeline.** Type a word to narrow the day to matching titles, programs, websites, notes, tags, categories or projects. `#word` looks at tags only.
- **Tags for many blocks at once.** Select blocks in the timeline and choose "# Tags" to add tags to all of them, or replace theirs.
- **Time per tag** in the HTML and JSON reports.
- **Keyboard shortcuts.** Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 open the pages, Alt+Left and Alt+Right change the day, Alt+Home goes back to today, Ctrl+F searches the timeline, Ctrl+N adds time, Ctrl+E exports the day in view, Ctrl+T starts or stops the timer, Enter confirms a form. Press F1 for the list.

### Changed

- Timesheets have a new last column, `billable` (CSV) and a `billable` field (JSON). The other columns are where they were.
- Time added by hand may run past midnight: "22:30 to 01:15" now means until 01:15 the next day.
- On the Projects page the keywords of all projects now line up in one column.
- The portable ZIP now includes this changelog.
- For people who build from source: `scripts\package.ps1` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

### Fixed

- **Settings could be lost after a damaged settings file.** If the settings file could not be read (for example after a crash while the disk was full), HourForge started with the defaults and the next change replaced your categories, rules and projects for good. The unreadable file is now kept next to it as `settings.damaged.json`.
- On the Today page, "Next day" could walk into days that have not happened yet. It now stops at today, as the timeline already did.

pulseforge.name: PulseForge 1.1.0
pulseforge.body:
### Added

- **Group processes by name.** Tick "Group by name" on the Processes page to get one row per program, with the processor, memory, disk and graphics use of all its processes added up and a count such as ×12. A browser with dozens of processes becomes a single line you can sort and compare.
- **Details of the selected process** under the table: which program started it, the user it runs as, how long it has been running, its handles and its graphics memory.
- **Drive encryption state.** The Storage page and the exported report now say for every volume whether it is encrypted with BitLocker. No administrator rights are needed.
- **Alert history that survives a restart.** The Alerts page keeps the last 200 alerts between runs, and a new Clear button empties the list.
- **Copy summary.** A button on the System page (or Ctrl+Shift+C) puts a short description of the computer on the clipboard: model, Windows version, processor, memory, graphics, drives and displays. It contains no serial numbers, names or addresses, so it is safe to paste into a message or a forum post.
- **Keyboard shortcuts.** Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+0 open the pages, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab step through them, Ctrl+F searches the processes, Ctrl+E exports a report, Ctrl+M switches the mini widget on or off and F5 reads the hardware and the drives again. They are listed in Settings and in the tooltips of the navigation.
- **Automatic clean-up of CSV logs.** A new "Keep the files" setting deletes log files older than 7, 30 or 90 days. The default is still to keep them for ever, and only PulseForge's own log files are ever removed.
- **Mini widget: back to the main window.** Double-click the widget, or right-click it and choose "Open PulseForge".
- **The window opens the way you left it**: at the same size and on the same page. The page part can be switched off in Settings ("Open where I left off").

### Changed

- Starting PulseForge while it is already running now shows the window of the running copy (also when it is hidden in the notification area) instead of starting a second copy with a second icon.
- The volume tables in the exported report have a new "Encryption" column.
- The empty alert history no longer says "since PulseForge started", because the history is now kept.
- For people who build from source: `scripts/package.ps1` now respects `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

### Fixed

- The notification-area icon could disappear while the window was hidden, leaving no way to bring PulseForge back. This happened when the icon was switched off in Settings, PulseForge was started in the notification area, and the mini widget was then switched from the icon's menu. The icon now always stays while the window is hidden.
- The mini widget could open outside the screen after the display it was left on had been unplugged. It now opens in a visible place.
- The "Encryption" column on the Storage page always said "Unknown".
- The Memory screenshot in the README was a broken image.

socketforge.name: SocketForge 1.1.0
socketforge.body:
### Added

- **Tools page** with two helpers that run inside SocketForge, need no administrator rights and change nothing in Windows:
  - **Serve a folder over HTTP.** Pick a folder and a port, press Start, and open `http://localhost:port/`. Folders without an `index.html` get a file listing. A list shows the latest requests. By default only this PC can connect; one checkbox lets other devices on your network connect too (a whole drive cannot be shared this way).
  - **Forward a local port.** Listen on a port of this PC and pass every connection on to another address, for example `localhost:15432` to a database on another machine. Shows open connections, totals and the last error. Several forwards can run at once.
- **Block-list import.** "Import a hosts file or block list" now understands hosts-style lists (`0.0.0.0 ads.example`), plain lists of names and `||ads.example^` filter rules. Names that are repeated in the list are added once, names your hosts file already has are left as they are, and you choose whether they point at `0.0.0.0` or `127.0.0.1`.
- **Remove duplicates** in the hosts editor's More menu: removes names that repeat an earlier line with the same address.
- **DNS cache tab** in the hosts editor: the names Windows currently remembers, with their record type, a search, a Flush button, and a button to add a name to the hosts file.
- **Notes and favourites for ports.** In the details panel, star a port and type a note such as "storefront dev server". The note shows in the table in place of the usual use of the port, the search finds it, and a Favourites filter shows only starred ports.
- **Right-click menu on hosts entries:** copy the names, the address or the line, switch on or off, edit, delete.
- A dot next to "Hosts file" in the side bar while there are unsaved changes.

### Changed

- **Large hosts files are fast now.** Files with more than 2,000 lines open in a quick, read-only raw view with line numbers that the search box filters; "Edit as text anyway" is one click away. The profiles tab and the import dialog no longer go through the whole file many times a second.
- Importing a long list takes a moment; it used to get slower with every line.
- The backups tab opens quickly even when the backups are large.
- The size limit for a hosts file is 32 MB everywhere (importing allowed 32 MB, but saving stopped at 16 MB).
- Large numbers of entries are written with thousands separators.
- `scripts\package.ps1` builds into `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when it is set.

### Fixed

- **Closing the window no longer drops unsaved hosts changes without a word.** SocketForge asks whether to save, close without saving, or stay. This also covers Exit from the notification area, and "Restart as administrator" asks you to save or revert first.
- A hosts file that is too large is refused before the backup is made and before the administrator prompt, with a clear message, instead of failing after you approved the prompt.
- If the administrator step takes longer than a minute, SocketForge says so instead of showing "code 259".
- Pressing Esc in a hosts dialog no longer also clears the search box.

veilforge.name: VeilForge 1.1.0
veilforge.body:
Everything you protected with 1.0.0 stays protected and opens as before. Nothing has to be unlocked before updating.

### Added

- **Kurdish, Arabic, Persian and Hebrew names are shown properly.** Letters are joined and the text runs in the right direction, the same way File Explorer shows it. This works in the list, the details panel, the dialogs, the messages and for group names.
- **A hotkey that locks everything.** Choose one in Settings (for example Ctrl+Alt+L). From anywhere, it locks every item you had opened for now and locks VeilForge itself.
- **`VeilForge.exe --lock-now`** does the same from a shortcut, a script or the Task Scheduler.
- **Ctrl+L** locks VeilForge while its window is in front.
- **Wrong-password log.** Every wrong master password is noted: when, and where it was typed (the VeilForge window, a protected item's password prompt, or "Restore everything"). What was typed is never stored. After you unlock, VeilForge tells you if someone tried while you were away. The list is in Settings, with a button to clear it.
- **The lock screen shows items that are still open.** If you opened items for now and VeilForge then locked itself, the lock screen says so and has a "Lock them now" button. Locking never needs the password.
- **Lock VeilForge when its window is closed** (a new setting, on by default).
- **The tray icon says what is going on** when the mouse rests on it: locked, unlocked, or how many items are open.
- **The details panel says when an open item locks again** on its own, following your settings.
- **Drop more files onto the open "Protect" dialog** to add them to its list. The drop hint also says how many items you are holding.

### Changed

- Closing the window to the tray now also locks VeilForge, so opening it again asks for the master password. You can switch this off in Settings, under "Locking again".
- "Lock now" in the tray menu now also reaches items that were opened through their stand-in shortcut while the main window was locked.
- The waiting time after wrong passwords is now shared by the window and the password prompts, and it carries on after VeilForge is closed and started again.
- The portable ZIP and the installer now include this changelog.

### Fixed

- A hotkey that Windows refused, because another program already uses it, was shown as "Active". It now says "Used by another program".
- Closing VeilForge and starting it again reset the waiting time after wrong passwords.
- Kurdish and Arabic file names appeared as separate letters in the wrong order.
- For developers: the packaging script now follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` instead of assuming the build is in `target`.

privacyforge.name: PrivacyForge 1.0.0
privacyforge.body:
First release of PrivacyForge, a Windows 10/11 privacy and debloat app.

- 135 privacy settings in 12 categories, each explained, read from your PC and marked Recommended, Limited or Not recommended
- Apply recommended with a full preview, an optional restore point and an undo journal
- Remove built-in Store apps for your account; Store, shell and frameworks are never offered
- Undo one change, one apply or everything; detects settings Windows put back and offers to re-apply
- Profiles (JSON), a text report, `--report` and `--apply-profile`
- No telemetry, no network requests

**Tested:** reading settings on a real PC, and the full apply / revert / undo cycle against a scratch registry key and an in-memory PC (55 unit tests plus `--selftest`). **Not yet run on a real PC:** applying settings, removing apps, the administrator prompt and restore points. Make a restore point before your first apply.

| File | |
|---|---|
| PrivacyForge-Setup.exe | Installer (no admin needed to install) |
| PrivacyForge-1.0.0-portable-x64.zip | Portable |
| PrivacyForge.exe | Bare 4.6 MB EXE |

metaforge.name: MetaForge 1.0.0
metaforge.body:
First release of MetaForge: see and remove hidden information in files before you share them.

- Photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF, GIF, HEIC/AVIF), documents (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODT/ODS/ODP, PDF, RTF), audio (MP3, FLAC, OGG, WAV, M4A) and video (MP4, MOV)
- Privacy badges per file, plain-language details, one-button cleaning with presets; photos cleaned without re-encoding; every result is read back and checked
- Edit common fields and GPS, file dates, rename from metadata, CSV/JSON export, compare two files
- Optional Explorer right-click entries (per user, removable), command line `--show` / `--clean` / `--export`
- No network requests, no telemetry, no administrator rights needed

Tested with generated sample files of every format (125 tests plus `--selftest`) and cross-checked with Pillow, pypdf and ffmpeg. Not yet tested: opening cleaned Office files in Word/Excel/PowerPoint/LibreOffice, real phone HEIC photos, the installer itself. Keep the default "save a copy" setting until you trust it with your own files.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MetaForge-Setup.exe` | Installer (per user) |
| `MetaForge-1.0.0-portable-x64.zip` | Portable |
| `MetaForge.exe` | The bare EXE |

displayforge.name: DisplayForge 1.0.0
displayforge.body:
First release of DisplayForge, monitor control for Windows.

- Brightness, contrast, volume, input, power, colour preset and RGB gain for external monitors over DDC/CI; brightness for laptop screens through Windows
- Tray panel: a slider per monitor, link all, presets (Day, Evening, Night, Reading), night light; mouse wheel over the tray icon
- Night light (1900-6500 K) and dimming below zero (gamma ramp or overlay)
- Daily schedule by clock time or sunrise/sunset (computed locally), with gradual transitions
- Per-app profiles, idle dimming, global hotkeys
- Display settings with a 15-second keep-or-revert, HDR and scaling status, EDID details, test patterns, identify
- Command line: --list, --brightness 40 [--monitor N], --preset Night

Tested so far: 133 unit tests and --selftest against simulated monitors; on real hardware only a laptop's built-in screen was read (nothing changed). DDC/CI monitors, gamma and display changes have not yet been tried on real hardware.

Files: DisplayForge-Setup.exe (installer, per-user, optional start with Windows), the portable ZIP, or the bare EXE. No administrator rights needed. No network requests.

powerforge.name: PowerForge 1.0.0
powerforge.body:
First release of PowerForge: battery health and history, power plans in plain language with automatic switching, keep-awake (timer, until a time, while an app runs, while downloads/copies are active), and sleep/wake diagnostics that explain what blocks sleep and what woke the PC.

- `PowerForge-Setup.exe`: per-user installer, optional start with Windows
- `PowerForge-1.0.0-portable-x64.zip`: portable
- `PowerForge.exe`: the bare EXE

Tested for real on a laptop: live battery readings, battery report, plan list, last wake, wake-capable devices, sleep states and event-log history. Plan changes, auto switching, device wake and hibernate toggles, and the administrator checks (what blocks sleep, wake timers, energy check) were tested against mock backends and sample output only. No telemetry, no network requests.

eventforge.name: EventForge 1.0.0
eventforge.body:
First release of EventForge: Windows event logs in plain language.

- Home overview: one clear status, a daily stability score for 30 days, and cards for blue screens, unexpected shutdowns, app crashes and hangs, failed updates, disk warnings, hardware errors, driver problems and slow startups
- Every problem explained: what happened, how serious (traffic light), likely cause and numbered steps; repeats grouped; technical details on request
- Knowledge base: 177 event IDs, 72 blue-screen stop codes, 62 Windows Update codes, 30 app crash codes
- Timeline, startup and shutdown history, app reliability ranking
- Masked HTML or text report for support; `--summary` and `--export` on the command line
- Read only, no telemetry, no network requests; optional notifications (off by default)

Tested on one Windows 11 PC without administrator rights. The administrator-only parts (startup times, sign-in counts, crash dump files) and naming a driver from a real crash dump have not been tested on real data yet.

| File | |
|---|---|
| EventForge-Setup.exe | Installer (no administrator rights needed) |
| EventForge-1.0.0-portable-x64.zip | Portable |
| EventForge.exe | The bare EXE |
